utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good morning. I would like to greet the parties, the accused, and all our staff, as well as our guests in the gallery. You have been informed that Judge Rodrigues is on an urgent mission and I will be presiding today. As for tomorrow and after tomorrow, Judge Wald will also be on an urgent mission so I will be the Presiding Judge. Now I would like our witness to take the oath, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Please be seated. Mr. Harmon, the witness is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Judge Riad, Judge Wald. Good morning to my colleagues for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, I'm going to be asking you a number of questions on direct examination, and following my examination you'll be asked questions by my colleagues from the Defence, and following their questions I'll ask you questions once again, and then the Judges will have an opportunity to ask you questions. Let me start, Mr. Erdemovic, by asking you how old you are.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I'm 28 and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: In Tuzla, a town called Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Croat, Bosnian Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you tell us about your educational background.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I went to a school for mechanical technicians. I'm a locksmith.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Before the war, then, you were a locksmith; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I hadn't been working yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I want to go into your history before this Tribunal. I don't want to go into all of the complex litigation that surrounded your case, but on the 14th of January, 1998, did you enter a guilty plea to one count of a violation of our Article 3, which was a violation of the laws and customs of war, specifically murder?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was that guilty plea pursuant to a plea agreement that was entered into between yourself and your counsel and representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, the underlying facts that supported your guilty plea was that you and members of your unit, along with soldiers from another unit of the Bosnian Serb army, did shoot and kill and did participate in the execution of unarmed Muslim men at the Branjevo Military Farm on the 16th of July, 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: On the 5th of March, 1998, were you sentenced by a Trial Chamber of this Tribunal to serve a term of five years' imprisonment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were you given credit for all of the time that you had been in custody, that is, from the time of March 28th, 1996 until the date of your judgement, your sentencing?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Have you now completed your term of imprisonment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You are testifying today freely and voluntarily; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President and Judge Wald, I would ask the Court to take judicial notice of its own records in this proceeding. There is an indictment and a sentencing judgement. I've had an opportunity to talk to my colleagues from the Defence and we discussed the issue of judicial notice, pursuant to Rule 94, and they have no objection to Your Honours taking such notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Erdemovic, I'd like to focus your attention on your own military background in the various armies that were in the former Yugoslavia. First of all, let me begin by asking you, did you serve in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How long of a period of time were you in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I was in the JNA for a year as my regular service, and then another four months in reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When did you finally leave the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: At the end of March 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: After leaving the JNA, did you return to your home in the Tuzla area?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: After you were in Tuzla, were you again called up by the JNA and asked to serve in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you serve in the JNA again or did you refuse?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I refused. I returned my call-up papers and said that I had already spent enough time in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you at any point in time, then, serve in the Territorial Defence in your village?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Describe the nature of that service. What kind of service was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: It was a service in our local community. At night we would walk around the village and keep guard in our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, did you eventually join the Armija, the army of the Bosnian Muslim government?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was in July 1992, I got a call-up to report to the barracks in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you respond to that call-up?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you serve in the Armija from July of 1992 until approximately October of 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you describe your duties and responsibilities while you were serving in the army.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I was a member of a reconnaissance unit on mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Where did you serve the majority of your time?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: In a position above Gornja Tuzla or Upper Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were you on the front lines most of the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, but as a reconnoitre.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, when you came to the Tribunal initially and you had a conversation with an investigator from my office, Jean-Rene Ruez, did you tell him that you had served in the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Subsequently, when you testified publicly under oath at the Rule 61 hearing in 1996, did you then testify about your service in the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, later did you volunteer to serve in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: In the military police of the HVO, in the village next to mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Why did you volunteer to serve in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Because I got a position in the military police, and because I didn't want to be exposed to danger on the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So had you become essentially tired of serving on the front lines and wanted to have a safer position?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, did you serve in the HVO from October of 1992 until November of 1993?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: While you were serving in the HVO, were you arrested?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you briefly explain to the Trial Chamber the circumstances of your arrest.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I was assisting civilians, Serbs from Tuzla, to cross into territory under the control of the army of Republika Srpska. In the first attempt I was not arrested, but in the second attempt, with a larger group of civilians who were mostly women and children, I was arrested on Mount Majevica by an HVO communications unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were you put in custody as a result of that arrest?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Ultimately were you released from custody, and did you return to the HVO military police to serve with them?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When they questioned me and when I told them everything, they beat me, mistreated me. They demanded that I admit certain things that I did not know of, some other attempts of transporting Serbs. I was questioned by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and their police, and after some time they turned me back to the HVO police, and I asked the head of the HVO police to let me go home to have a bath and change my uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When the head of the military police released me I went home, and I met a neighbour, a Serb, who asked me whether I could help him to cross into the territory held by the Serbs. I told him, "You know that I'm arrested, and if I'm arrested again I won't fare well." He told me then, and my wife was with me at the time, that he would help me go to Switzerland because his sons are working in Switzerland and I wouldn't have to spend much time in Republika Srpska. After thinking it over, I agreed to that because I wanted to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you then leave to the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When did you arrive in the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: On the 3rd of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When I reached Serb territory I was questioned by the command, which was headquartered in Lopare, at the foot of Mount Majevica. Regarding the group I had transferred, this group had told them that I had been correct towards the Serbs and that I was correct with everyone. And after a day long of questioning, in the evening they told me that the next day I would be released, as well as my wife and those two other persons who were of Croat ethnicity and who were with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If could you describe very briefly, Mr. Erdemovic, what you did from that point on until the point in time when you joined the army of the Republika Srpska. I don't want to go into great detail, but could you just tell the Judges in outline form what you did, where you went, and how you ended up in the army of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When I reached Bijeljina, I started having problems with paramilitary units, of which certain people from Tuzla were members, they were Serbs, and they mistreated me. And this man who promised to help me go to Switzerland simply turned his back on me and my wife and said, "I can't help you." I had no other choice. But a Croat who was with me called up his relative who was living in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, in Titov Vrbas, and he came about a day later to Bijeljina to take us to Titov Vrbas. I couldn't stay in Bijeljina at that time because they were threatening me. They said I had to join a paramilitary unit or simply that I couldn't stay on, I would be killed. So my wife, the two Croats, and I, and this man who came to collect us from Titov Vrbas, we they went to Titov Vrbas to stay with him. That was also in the month of November. After that, I can't remember exactly, but I think we stayed in Titov Vrbas until January, my wife and I and these two Croats. As we had no money, we simply couldn't stay with these people, enjoying their hospitality, as they too were not well-off. After a while, I think it was in January of 1994, police raids started in Serbia, so people who were not from Serbia and who were from Bosnia had to go back to Bosnia. So with my wife, I decided to go back to Republika Srpska, to stay with her uncle in Trebinje. We called him up from Serbia and he told us to come. He knew I was a Croat, and still he said that we could come. When we reached Trebinje, at the border between Serbia and Republika Srpska, the police identified me by my ID card, and he said, "You're not a Serb. Your name is not Serbian, nor is your father's name." I said I wasn't a Serb but that I was a Croat, but my wife was a Serb. They let us go and told me to report immediately to the police station in Foca. I didn't report immediately. I went to my wife's uncle's with her. I didn't report because I didn't know where the police station in Foca was. It was my first time in Foca. We went to a place close to Foca called Miljevina, where my wife's uncle was. And the next day we went to the police station, and this man treated me very kindly, he wasn't arrogant or anything. He said I couldn't stay in Foca because there were no Croats or Muslims there, that I should go back to Bijeljina. Of course I had to tell him the whole story, how I got to Foca. He said I had to go back to Bijeljina where I had crossed to leaving Tuzla. So I returned to Bijeljina. This must have been the beginning of April. In Bijeljina I met a friend of mine whom I knew from before, from Tuzla, he was a Serb, he was a nice man. I even stayed with him for a while. He was very kind. I explained everything that had happened, where I had been and everything. He told me I couldn't achieve any rights in Republika Srpska, I wouldn't even be able to move around without a permit if I was not in the army. So I decided to report to the army. I went to the military department in Bijeljina. I had to tell them again this whole story from the time I left Tuzla, and they told me that a unit had been formed consisting of Croats and Muslims who had crossed over from Tuzla to Bijeljina, and who had also been helping Serbs. And when I asked them where this unit was, they told me it wasn't far from Bijeljina, a place called Dvorovi. I went there and I recognised some Croats whom I had known from Tuzla, from before. I spoke to them, and they told me that they would help me join this unit, and after a few days, I did in fact join the unit, which then was not called the 10th Sabotage Detachment but was a special unit of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, when you joined this special detachment, how many men were in it?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Eight.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did this special unit evolve into the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in October 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you tell the Judges what kind of unit was the 10th Sabotage Detachment.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: It was a sabotage unit which would go into the rear of the enemy and blow up munition warehouses, artillery storages, and that sort of thing. That is what we did behind the enemy lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So you were an infiltration and sabotage unit.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, turning our attention to July of 1995, can you tell me approximately how many men were in the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean the whole detachment?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I was able to assess, there could have been about 60 men. I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, was the 10th Sabotage Detachment subordinate to the Main Staff of the Bosnian Serb army?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you describe to the Judges the structure of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, how many platoons there were, where they were located?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: There were two platoons; one was in Bijeljina and the other was in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, how large, how many men were in each of those respective platoons?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think in Bijeljina there were about 30 men. I don't know about Vlasenica. But perhaps a similar number, three or four or five men less, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let's focus your attention on the Bijeljina platoon that was part of the 10th Sabotage Detachment. Of those approximately 30 men, how many of those men were involved in infiltration and sabotage activities, and how many of those 30 men were rear services people who would support your activities?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think that in the infiltration and sabotage activities, there were about 22 men, roughly, I would say. I don't know the exact number of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did the remaining men then participate in rear service activities, support activities?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you tell us who the commander of the Bijeljina platoon was?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: It was Franc Kos.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did he have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: We called him Slovenac, the Slovene, or Zuco, we used to call him Zuco.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the Vlasenica platoon?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I only know that they called him Lule. I don't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'd like you to then identify some of the hierarchy of the 10th Sabotage Detachment as you knew it in July of 1995. Could you please tell us, from the highest levels working down to the level of Franc Kos and Lule, what was the reporting chain of command?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, in first place there was Colonel Salapura from the Main Staff, the intelligence centre, he was there from the beginning when there were eight of us, and later on as well. Under him, I think I got to know in March 1995, Major Pecanac. Underneath Pecanac, there was Milorad Pelemis; he was First Lieutenant. Underneath Pelemis, there was Radoslav Kremenovic, who was a First Lieutenant who came to the unit in 1995; sometime in February, I don't know exactly. Underneath Kremenovic, there was Slovenac in Bijeljina who was the platoon commander, and Lule in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you participated in some sabotage and infiltration activities, as did other members of your unit. When your unit travelled to an area in the Republika Srpska that was under the command of, say, the Drina Corps or a brigade, what was the procedure, if any, to notify the other members of the VRS that you were going to be operating in and out of their territory? Could you tell the Judges, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I know for certain what the situation was like at Mount Majevica, and that was the zone of responsibility of the Majevica Brigade. Before we would start out from Bijeljina, the commander, or leader, would have to inform the command which was in that area of responsibility that we were coming, and what time we would be coming. I don't know that -- I know that they didn't speak of the actual operations that would take place in that territory, and when I say "The zone of responsibility," it is a broader area. So they would be informed of our arrival and that we would have to undertake operations in that zone of responsibility. They didn't actually say what operations we would be undertaking, but we had to inform them because otherwise we could not pass into their zone of responsibility and move around if the command had not been informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So informing them was, in part, to ensure your own safety; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, both our safety and theirs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, when you conducted these operations, these sabotage and infiltration operations, normally did you conduct them with members of your unit alone, or were they joint operations? When I say "joint operations," Mr. Erdemovic, I'm talking about operations with members of, say, a brigade or another company? What was the routine, the normal modis operandi?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: In the areas where we knew for certain where we were supposed to pass and what we were supposed to do, we worked alone. But there were operations, for example, when we entered through an underground pit between Bratunac and Srebrenica, then we were led by a group which was from Bratunac because we didn't know this mine very well, and there were several corridors and we might have lost our way had we done it alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In the operation that you just testified about, when members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment went into a mine, because they were unfamiliar with the various tunnels, they received assistance from people from the brigade who had been miners and were familiar with the mine routes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: But other than give you guidance in the mines, those people didn't participate in the operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I want to focus your attention now to the attack on Srebrenica itself that took place in July of 1995, and, particularly, I want to focus your attention on the role of the 10th Sabotage Detachment in that attack. Could you tell the Judges on what date your unit, the 10th Sabotage Detachment, deployed to the area of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: On the 10th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: In the evening hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: From whom did you receive your deployment orders?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: In the morning we received orders from the commander of the platoon, Franc Kos, in Bijeljina, that we should prepare to move into action.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Then you arrived on the night of the 10th, is that correct, in the Srebrenica area.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, but we weren't told beforehand where we would be going until we actually got there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How many members of your platoon were deployed to the area of Srebrenica to participate in the assault on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think between 15 and 20. I'm not quite sure of the exact number. That's what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, commence an assault on Srebrenica on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you receive any special instructions prior to the assault from any of your superior officers?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the morning of the 11th, Pelemis came and told us that in no case should be fire at civilians and that we should send the civilians off to the football stadium at Srebrenica. He told us on the occasion that the resistance would probably be strong and that at the first mosque would be the first resistance, that is to say, at the entrance into town.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, when you participated in the assault, did you do this only with members of your unit, the 10th Sabotage Detachment, or did you participate in the operation with a unit that was part of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Pelemis said that we would be joined by some 15 men, I think about 15 men, from the Drina Wolves.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you know the Drina Wolves were part of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, you told us earlier in your testimony that normally the 10th Sabotage Detachment operated exclusively with its own men. On this occasion, on the assault on Srebrenica, you're telling us that you worked with another unit, part of the Drina Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And this seemed to us to be a little unusual because we were used to working on our own. But another thing that seemed strange to me and unusual was that we were not a unit to take control of the town. We were intended for sabotage operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So your normal mission for your unit had changed from sabotage to one of being part of the invading or the assaulting force; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, what was the objective of your group's operation? Were you informed of what your objective was and what the Drina Wolves, who were working with you, what was their objective?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Pelemis told us that it was our objective to enter the town first with these people, and when he told us that he said that, "On your left-hand side," I can't quite remember who would be on the left and right, but I know that he mentioned Sekovici, Bratunac, Milici, Vlasenica, so that once we descend into town they would descend too from the surrounding hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When you say Sekovici, Vlasenica, Milici, and Bratunac, are you referring to the brigades from Sekovici, Vlasenica, Milici, and Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: He said units. He didn't use the word brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So units from those --

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: -- I take it units from those brigades would follow your penetration into Srebrenica, and after there had been penetration by your group and the Drina Wolves, then the brigade groups would follow; is that how I understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who was the commander, to your knowledge, of the Drina Wolves?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I just know that his nickname was Legenda, legend.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who was the leader of the group of the 10th Sabotage Detachment that went with you in the direction of Srebrenica? Was it Lieutenant Pelemis?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did Legenda also participate in the assault on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did he and Lieutenant Pelemis communicate in order to coordinate their efforts?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because at one point Pelemis, that is to say, Legenda was to our left -- on raised ground to our left. At one moment Pelemis told us that we should set fire to the first thing next to us. For the artillery, the tank, and heavy machine-guns, to shoot at the surrounding hills and not at us, so that they could know the point where we had reached.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could have the assistance of the usher, and if the usher could place on the ELMO for the witness Prosecutor's Exhibit 4A, which is a map. I'm not getting the image on my monitor. I don't know if Your Honours are getting the image. It appears that the ELMO is not working, and we're going to need the ELMO throughout the testimony of Mr. Erdemovic. Perhaps we can have the assistance of the technical people to see if this monitor could be made functional today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: It's being taken care of.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It is? Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, could you proceed with your questioning in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm going to quickly start to get to the point where he's going to need some exhibits to illustrate his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'll ask you some questions. Mr. Erdemovic, let me ask you, you had been informed by Lieutenant Pelemis that your group and the Drina Wolves could anticipate heavy resistance. Did you, in fact, get heavy resistance?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you describe to the Judges the manner in which your group divided? How many different groups of 10th Sabotage and Drina Wolves were there that advanced onto Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: There were four groups in our detachment. The Drina Wolves, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. But your group, consisting of Drina Wolves and 10th Sabotage Detachment soldiers, divided into four groups and advanced in the direction of the town of Srebrenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I had asked that Prosecutor's Exhibit 4A, which is a map, be placed on the ELMO because I wanted you to illustrate and inform the Judges the direction in which you approached Srebrenica. Without that map, perhaps you can just describe, did you approach the town of Srebrenica from the south of the town?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Oh, here it's working finally. Now, if we could have that so the town of Srebrenica is shown on the ELMO. There we go. Move it up a little, please. That's fine right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, using the pointer, Mr. Erdemovic, could you illustrate to the Judges the direction which your four groups took in the assault on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: This direction here [indicates], towards the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating, for the record, Mr. Erdemovic placed the pointer initially at the juncture of the hairpin turn and moved it toward the top of the exhibit, in the direction of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So you moved from the south of the town, toward the centre of town; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, if I could have Prosecutor's Exhibit 4/4 placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, Mr. Erdemovic, reach the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know for sure whether it was the centre of town, but that's what I assumed at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me show you Prosecutor's Exhibit 4/4, and this is a photograph of part of the town of Srebrenica. Is this the location that you considered or thought was the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, here [indicates], that is the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was there a mosque in the general vicinity where you have just pointed?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating, for the record, it looks like a platform with a circle in the middle of it that is directly located in the centre of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was that mosque that you observed on the morning of -- on the 11th of July, was it intact? Was it standing?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When you entered the town, had you passed another mosque?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the beginning, when we moved off. It wasn't far from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was that mosque standing as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived in the location that you've pointed on Prosecutor's Exhibit 4/4, could you tell the Judges what happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When we arrived there, a civilian, wearing civilian clothing, surrendered and said, "I was never in the army." He was about 30 years old, tall; he wasn't fat, as far as I could see, he was thin.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: To whom had he surrendered?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Because we were the first to descend into town, he surrendered to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, did it appear to you that -- other than that one individual that you saw, was the town abandoned?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But we called people to come out of their houses and to move in front of us, towards the stadium. People did come out, I don't know how many, but most of them were elderly people who found it difficult to walk.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let's continue focusing on this young man who had surrendered. What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Later on, when we had already got there, the units descended from the surrounding hills and one particular group started to mistreat that young man, to beat him with rifles, with their fists, kick him and so on. And after that, perhaps a minute or two after all of that abuse, Pelemis ordered one of the soldiers to go and slit that man's throat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did, in fact -- first of all, can you identify the man who was ordered to go slit the captive's throat?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Zoran. Zoran, nicknamed Maljic, from Vlasenica. I don't know his family name.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did Zoran follow the order of Lieutenant Pelemis and slit this young man's throat?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you use the pointer, please, again referring to Prosecutor's Exhibit 4/4, and point where in this picture the execution occurred?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Here [indicates], in between these two buildings here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating two buildings that are on the left-hand side of the exhibit, slightly above a curve in the road that appears in the centre of Prosecutor's Exhibit 4/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. That's fine. Thank you, Mr. Erdemovic. Now, what happened? Did that man's body remain in the location where it had dropped?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It remained there on the pavement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask the usher to please bring two exhibits: Prosecutor's Exhibit 28/17 and Prosecutor's Exhibit 147.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you know why Lieutenant Pelemis gave the order to Maljic to kill this man, particularly since he had earlier given an order that no civilians were to be hurt?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know why but I think it was because he was -- because he was fit for military service. That's what I think, but I don't know exactly. I'm not aware of the actual reason. It looked a little strange, particularly in view of the fact that he had told us not to touch anybody, and after having said that he ordered us to slit this man's throat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. We're going to start with one exhibit. I'm still waiting for another exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you place that on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me ask you, this photograph has two individuals marked, one with the number 1 and one with the number 2. Do you see Zoran Maljic, the man who executed the Muslim civilian who was in the custody of your unit? And could you point him out, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating, for the record, in Prosecutor's Exhibit 147, the man with the number 2 on his shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, in that same picture there is a man with the number 1 marked on his shoulder. Do you see that man, Mr. Erdemovic, and can you identify him for the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is the leader of the platoon from Bijeljina, Franc Kos [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Perhaps we can use my exhibit. I can use the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me show you what is Prosecutor's Exhibit 28/17, and I ask that that be placed on the ELMO, please. Now, Mr. Erdemovic, you've mentioned Lieutenant Pelemis who gave the order to execute the young man in Srebrenica. Do you see him in this particular picture? Can you point him out, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating, for the record, the man on the right-hand side of that picture being Lieutenant Pelemis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Erdemovic. Thank you, Mr. Usher, that's all I need. Now, after this young man was executed, Mr. Erdemovic, were you given an order by Lieutenant Pelemis to do anything?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He told us to go back. At the time I didn't know it was the southern part of the town of Srebrenica. Anyway, he told us to go back to where we had come from and to provide security at the entrance of the town. He told this to me and other members of my unit. On the way back he told me to report to him when General Mladic reaches the town, General Mladic and the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So at the point of town when you were in the centre, General Mladic, General Krstic, and General Zivanovic had not arrived in town yet; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you follow Lieutenant Pelemis' order, and did you go to the entrance of the town in the south and did you set up a position?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were you with other members of your unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I forgot to ask you one question, and that is this: Going back to the beginning of the assault, when your unit started the assault on Srebrenica, approximately what time was that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say now exactly. But when NATO bombs dropped, I think, two bombs, a man from our unit looked at his wristwatch and said that it was about ten past eleven, I think. We had already reached the first mosque in town by that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me take you back to the location where you were at the southern entrance of the town, waiting for the arrival of General Mladic. Your instructions were to notify Lieutenant Pelemis that General Mladic had passed your point. How were you to do that? How were you to communicate with Lieutenant Pelemis?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: With a radio link, a Motorola. We called it the 1000.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now I'm going to play for Your Honours a film, which will be Prosecutor's Exhibit 148.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, you've seen this film before. I'm going to ask you a number of questions about it after you've had an opportunity to see this. This is a film that was taken outside of the town of Srebrenica, on the 11th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So if we could dim the lights, please, and if we could play Prosecutor's Exhibit 148. Unfortunately, Mr. President and Your Honours, I have no transcript for this film. One will follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dubuisson, perhaps the next time we have a film one should dim the rights a little.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, the location where that film was taken, specifically where the Dutch UNPROFOR APC was on its side, was that at a location that was outside of the town and away from the location where you had set up your checkpoint, pursuant to the order of Lieutenant Pelemis?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, if I could have Prosecutor's Exhibits 152, 153, 154, 155, 156, and 157 given to the usher, we're going to show those in order. They are new exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In the meantime, Mr. Erdemovic, having seen that film, did you see on that film a number of members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment present in the area where General Krstic was, where General Mladic was, where Colonel Pandurevic was and other representatives of the VRS army? Could you members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment there?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I saw three members of the 10th Sabotage Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a series of exhibits. We're going to start with Prosecutor's Exhibit 152.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All of these exhibits, Judge Riad and Judge Wald, are still images taken from the video we have just seen. They are not of the best quality but they are the best quality we could obtain.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me ask you, then, placing Prosecutor's Exhibit 152 on the ELMO, there are three individuals with yellow dots, 1, 2, and 3. Did you, in looking at this film, have the ability to identify the individuals 1, 2, and 3 as being members of your unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So all three of these individuals are members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the 10th Sabotage Detachment, belonging to the Vlasenica platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let's start with number 1. Can you identify the man who is number 1?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: He was a liaison officer, a signals officer, but I just know his name was Bujo. That was his nickname, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of the man who is number 2?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: But you know him to be a member of the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He worked in the signals section.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And number 3, can you identify him, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was also in the Vlasenica platoon formally, but sometimes he drove our commander Milorad Pelemis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is his name?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Cico.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We can turn to the next exhibit, Mr. Usher, that is Prosecutor's Exhibit 153.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The man with the yellow dot on his chest, is he a member of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, Mr. Erdemovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. His name is Bujo, and on the previous picture he was marked with the number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, in some of these images you'll see people with ribbons on their sides. Could you tell, first of all, the Chamber, did members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment receive ribbons before they started the assault and what the purpose of those ribbons was?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: In the morning, when we were about to enter town, we would receive red ribbons which we attached on our left shoulder, some maybe on the right. I don't know. But anyway we had to have those red ribbons so that we could be identified amongst the different units.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let's turn to the next image, which is 154. There are two individuals on Prosecutor's Exhibit 154 with a yellow dot on them, 1 and 2. Are both of those members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, even though one of these individuals has his back to us in this image, were you able to identify that individual in the film?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is Cico, the man nicknamed Cico.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment normally issued blue helmets?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is that helmet that Cico is wearing a UN helmet?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, the individual marked number 1 on this exhibit, a member of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is a member of the 10th Sabotage Detachment. He worked in the signals department but I don't know his first or last name or his nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Now we'll turn to the next image, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 155. There is a man with a yellow dot.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If you could move that image over, please, Mr. Usher, so you can see the complete image of that man. If you could move it up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, the man with the yellow dot is wearing, it looks like a grey T-shirt and green camouflage pants. Is that the normal outfit for the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the normal uniform worn by the members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: We wore a black uniform, the uniform worn by the army of Republika Srpska, and uniforms worn by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and by the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: But in terms of this operation that took place on the 11th of July, were members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment dressed in black, and were they also dressed in camouflage uniforms of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Most were dressed in black uniforms but some had camouflage uniforms as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let's focus -- let me focus your attention on the man in this photograph holding, it looks like, a blue helmet and has a blue beret under his belt and has a yellow dot on his chest. Can you tell the Judges, first of all, is he a member of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, and can you identify him by name?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He is a member of the 10th Sabotage Detachment. His name is Cico, or rather his nickname. I'm not sure whether it was his name or nickname, but that's how they called him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let us turn now to the next exhibit, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 156, another still image taken from the video we've just seen. And in the upper right-hand corner, Your Honours, is the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me ask you to direct your attention to the man in the middle with the yellow dot. Is that man a member of the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is his name?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: His name is Zoran Stupar. He comes from the Vlasenica detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Finally in this series of exhibits, let me turn your attention to Prosecutor's Exhibit 157. In this image is the accused and General Mladic and other representatives of the Bosnian Serb army. Do you recognise any of these people, and did you recognise any of these people on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I recognised on that day only General Mladic. I didn't know the other people, and I never met Mr. Krstic. The same applies to the person on Mladic's right-hand side, I never met him, but I heard of the surname Pandurevic in the Drina unit. But I had never heard of Mr. Krstic, nor did I ever see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm finished with this series of exhibits, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let's return to your testimony. Mr. Erdemovic, before I showed you this series of exhibits, you told us you'd gone up to a particular location and you were to inform Lieutenant Pelemis of the arrival of General Mladic. Did they, in fact, did General Mladic and other vehicles pass your location on the 11th --

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: -- I'm sorry. On the 12th of July. I'm sorry. On the 11th of July.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Approximately what time?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't have a watch so I don't know exactly, but when we reached the centre of town, then after that -- after the raid, the bombing raid, maybe two or three hours later.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, on the film that we have just seen, there was -- part of the images were of three vehicles descending a road, one of which contained General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: On the 11th of July, at your location did you see those vehicles and did those vehicles pass your location?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, were those vehicles then driving in the direction of the centre -- toward the centre of the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They went in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. President and Judge Wald, I'm not sure when you want to take a break, but I have only a few more minutes of this particular line of examination, and if we could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Would 11.00 be all right with you, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: We will have a break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm going to show Your Honours, it would be my next exhibit, Prosecutor's Exhibit 145. There are going to be two clips in this exhibit. It's a very short film; it lasts about 50 seconds with the total of the two, so one has to watch fairly quickly. If we could then dim the lights and if we could play Prosecutor's Exhibit 145.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now we'll show the second film. That should continue, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: How will we know what is being said?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I will submit a transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You have to go back on that portion of the film, please. It may be just as easy to start and show the whole thing again. Both segments last 51 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I think that's fine, Judge Riad. As I said, it was a very short film.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you now, Mr. Erdemovic. You've seen that film in my office. Is the location of where that film was taken, is that in the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, between the position that I was at and the very centre of town, or rather what I assumed was the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, in that film that you saw, did you see members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could show you, with the assistance of the usher, Prosecutor's Exhibit 158, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If that could be placed on the ELMO. In this exhibit, Mr. Erdemovic, there are three individuals marked with yellow dots, 1, 2, and 3. The accused is on the left-hand side of this image. Are the individuals marked with 1, 2, and 3 members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you identify them by name, starting with individual 1 and working toward individual number 3?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Number 1 is Velimir Popovic from the Bijeljina platoon. Number 2 is a man from the Vlasenica platoon whom I didn't want to mention in my earlier testimony, and if it is not absolutely essential, I would rather not today either. I didn't want to mention his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Well, unless I have -- but you know him to be a member of the 10th Sabotage Detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If the Defence ask you a question or if the Judges ask you to identify him, you will be required to identify him by name, Mr. Erdemovic. Let's move on to the number 3, please. Who is the individual with the number 3 marked on his body?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Stanko Savanovic from the Bijeljina platoon, a member of the 10th Sabotage Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to focus your attention if you would, Mr. Erdemovic, just briefly, on the man with the number 2, and on the left-hand shoulder of that individual there is a ribbon. Is that the kind of ribbon that you said was placed on the shoulders of the individuals who participated in the assault on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can see there is a ribbon but I cannot see that it is red. But I assume that that is the ribbon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Below the ribbon there's a patch, an insignia, on the man's left arm. Do you recognise that patch?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is the patch of the 10th Sabotage Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Lastly, turning your attention to number 3, the individual marked with the number 3, he's wearing a camouflage uniform, not a black uniform. Do you know why he was dressed --

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: -- differently from your other colleagues in the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think in the morning, when we set off from Bijeljina, he was wearing that uniform and that is how he remained. Whether he had a reserve uniform in his bag or not, a black uniform or some other uniform such as that of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Judge Riad, I'm at a point where it would be convenient to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, how long do you foresee your examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Approximately, two more hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Two more hours. We'll have a break of 20 minutes now and then another break at 12.40. We have to adjourn at 14.10 today. So at 11.20 we'll be back here. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If you could move that exhibit down just a little bit, please, Mr. Usher. Down a little more. A little more, please. That's fine right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, just before we took the break, you had been testifying about Prosecutor's Exhibit 158, and I wanted to ask you, are you familiar with this specific location where this image was taken?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, sometime after General Mladic drove by you, your position, with the other vehicles, did you go down to this specific location that is found in Prosecutor's Exhibit 158?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: At that particular location, when you went down there, did you find members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment present?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were they with a man who you did not know?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Before I get into what you observed and what you heard at that location, can you identify the members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment who you found at this particular location?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Under number 1, Velimir Popovic. Under number 2, an individual whom I did not wish to mention in my previous testimony, I didn't want to mention his name and I don't wish to mention his name today either and involve him in everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Under number 3 is Stanko Savanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you see any other members of your detachment at that location when you went down there?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who else?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Opposite on the pavement, Koljevrat Dragan was sitting down, and somebody else was with him. I don't remember exactly who.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you describe to the Judges what you saw when you went down to this position, what you heard.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When I got to this position, I saw Velimir Popovic, under number 1, the individual wearing number 2, and I didn't mention his name, and under number 3, Stanko Savanovic. Opposite was Dragan Koljevrat, and they were all members of the unit. With them there was just one individual whom I didn't know. When I asked who the man was, Stanko Savanovic said that it was the commander of the Drina Corps by the name of Zivanovic. And then the man with number 2 on him, whose name I did not mention, said he's not a general, he's not a commander, he's --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat that word, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: -- he was drunk. And there was a jerrycan with some alcohol, and it was tied to the battery of the car. The man I did not know, I saw a hand launcher which I had not seen before, of the type I hadn't seen, and he said, "Who's that?" And Savanovic said, "I found it in a house here." And I gave it to the General -- I asked why he had given it to the General and he said, "Because he's going to retire soon."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, what were these men drinking?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They were drinking, we call it in Bosnian, Slivovitz.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Which is plum brandy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Out of what kind of container were they drinking from?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They were drinking from a plastic jerrycan.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to have Prosecutor's Exhibit 28/4 placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, the interpreters did not hear the grade of Stanko Zivanovic. They said he was not a general, he was not a commander, and it was left open, an empty space there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you repeat, Mr. Erdemovic, what was said about Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Stanko Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: He said he was the commander -- Zivanovic said that he was the commander of the Drina Corps, and to that the individual under number 2 answered that -- he said, "He's not a commander but he's an alcoholic," and everybody laughed at that and I did too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What was the reason that was given to you why the rocket launcher was given to this man?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Because he was going to be retired soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I have placed on the ELMO Prosecutor's Exhibit 28/4. Do you see the man Zivanovic, who was drinking at the barricade with you and other members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, in this particular exhibit?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating, for the record, the second individual from the right-hand side of the image. Thank you, Mr. Erdemovic, and thank you, Mr. Usher. I have finished with that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, I'm going to turn your attention now to the 12th of July. Can you tell us approximately what time you and members of your unit left Srebrenica and returned to Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think that it was around noon, that is to say, in the morning hours, between 10.00 and 12.00. That's when we left Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Prior to leaving, where had you and members of your unit been billeted?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me what you mean by "where"? Do you mean where we spent the night?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Where you spent the night and where you spent the morning hours of the 12th.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: We spent the night on the southern side, where I was located, where we provided security to the entrance into town. There were two houses there; one was a large house and the other one was a little smaller.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you and did members of your group remain together until your departure on the morning of the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, at any time on the 12th of July, Mr. Erdemovic, did you or did members of your unit enter the town of Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could have the usher's assistance once again, please, if we could use Prosecutor's Exhibit 1/E/1 which is an A3-sized map, and if that could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to look at this map, Mr. Erdemovic, and I'm going to ask you to use the pointer and indicate for the Judges the location where you were and where you went and the route of your travel. And if we could move that up on the ELMO, please. That's fine right there. Could you use the pointer, Mr. Erdemovic, and just follow the line along your route of travel when you returned to Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: We went this away [indicates], towards Milici, roundabout over Rudnik, and that was an open pit mine, I think here [indicates], this part of the mine. I don't know the territory very well but I think it was. And when we passed by, there was some machinery there and this sort of mining equipment. So from Srebrenica we went along this route [indicates], the roundabout route to Milici, and from Milici we continued on to Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating for the record, they travelled south from Srebrenica, passed Zeleni Jadar, up the road towards Milici and then over towards Vlasenica. Thank you very much, Mr. Erdemovic. Mr. Usher, I've finished with that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, did you return to your base in Bijeljina or did you remain in Vlasenica on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: We remained in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Why didn't you go to Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to focus your attention, Mr. Erdemovic, on the time frame between the 13th of July and the 15th of July, and I don't want to go into great detail but I'd like you to tell the Judges in summary form where you and where certain members of your unit went and why you went to that particular location.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th, when we returned to Vlasenica, we were late because our truck -- there was something wrong with our truck and our unit was already there. When we came to Vlasenica, at midnight on the 12th, we learned that Pelemis had overturned, that is to say, the commander of the unit Pelemis had overturned with an APC not far from Vlasenica and our own base. Our own base was on the road leading from Vlasenica to Kladanj, the Vlasenica-Kladanj road. On that occasion, a soldier had lost his life, and he was Dragan Koljevrat and he was from Trebinje by birth. On the 13th, in the morning when we got up, a man who was in charge of the rear for our unit came up to me and said that I was to attend the funeral, along with some others, because I was a good friend of his and I was the leader of his group at one point in Bijeljina. And that was on the morning of the 13th. We went to Trebinje, I myself, the individual who drove the vehicle, and it was the driver under number 2, and five or six others. I don't remember exactly who they were but I think that's more or less how it was. So we left on the 13th to Trebinje, and as the journey was a long one, we had to pass by -- roundabout Sarajevo and the road had been destroyed by the war. We had to go through the forests, and we arrived in Trebinje on the 14th, in the morning, in the early morning hours, perhaps 4.00 or 5.00 a.m., I'm not quite sure. But that particular day we spent in Trebinje. The funeral was on the 14th, so that in the late afternoon hours, towards evening, we went towards Vlasenica, and because the road was so bad we arrived there on the 15th in the morning, once again at 5.00, 6.00, or 7.00 a.m., thereabouts. I don't know exactly but it was the early hours of the morning. And of course because we had spent the night of the 10th outside our house, and on the 11th and 12th I didn't get much sleep because we were travelling around until midnight, and the next day, the 13th, I attended the funeral; on the 14th, I was at the funeral; on the 15th, the whole night I spent travelling, so that on the night of the 15th, me and all the others who were with me slept for the most part of the day, until the late afternoon, 5.00 or 6.00, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, in relation to Vlasenica, where is Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Trebinje is situated south, southwards in Herzegovina, in the vicinity of the town of Dubrovnik, which is in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Erdemovic, we're now going to turn our attention to the 16th of July. On the 16th of July, did you and did members of your unit receive a new assignment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: From whom did you receive the assignment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Brano Gojkovic came and told us, told me, Franc Kos, and Zoran Goronja that we should prepare for our assignment. And when he asked him who said that we should go, he said that the order had been issued by Pelemis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, how many people were --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We've lost the English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear the English?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I can hear the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Judge Wald is bilingual. It's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How many members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment received an assignment on this morning of the 16th?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Eight.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you name the eight individuals who went on this particular assignment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Brano Gojkovic, Aleksandar Cvetkovic, who drove the vehicle that we were in, it was our unit's van; Golijan Vlastimir; Franc Kos; Zoran Goronja; Stanko Savanovic; and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You mentioned Marko Boskic.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. Sorry. Yes, there was him too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, these individuals were some members of the Bijeljina platoon and some of the Vlasenica platoon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you name the individuals in this assignment who were part of the Vlasenica platoon?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Brano Gojkovic, Aleksandar Cvetkovic, and Vlastimir Golijan.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And the other members of this group were members of your platoon; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who was the leader of this group?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Brano organised everything for us to pack, take all the equipment necessary for the operation. He was the leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, was the purpose of the operation explained to you while you were in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. We were only told that we were going into an operation of some kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Where did you go from Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: From Vlasenica we went in the general direction of Zvornik, and we stopped in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could have Prosecutor's Exhibits 170, 171, and 172 placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'll wait until they are distributed to the Judges before I ask you some questions about these. Let's start, Mr. Erdemovic, with Prosecutor's Exhibit 170. You said you went to Zvornik. Can you identify the location in Prosecutor's Exhibit 170 as being the location where you went?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me show you the next two exhibits. Exhibit 171, is this another view of the location where you went?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Lastly, 172, if that could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is that also the location where you and other members of your unit went in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was in the compound there. I don't know how many buildings like this were there, but I do know that that was the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if we could go back to 171, please. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Erdemovic, tell the Judges what happened when you arrived at this location.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When we arrived here, in front of this ramp [indicates], the ramp was opened up for us and our vehicle entered. Only Brano got out of the car, and the driver, and they went off in this administrative building, reception area. And there were two military policemen at the reception area. In front of these buildings here [indicates], there were quite a number of military policemen. Perhaps there were other forms of police as well, perhaps civilian, but all I know is that there were a lot of military policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, the reception area, for the record, the witness pointed to the structure on the far right, in the foreground. And when he said there were a lot of military policemen present, he was pointing to the smaller building in the background that's directly behind the gate that is open.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, what did Brano Gojkovic do? Do you know what he did when he went into this building? Did you go with him, or did he go in there alone?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. We all stayed in the van. Just he and Cvetkovic went inside, and that was the driver of the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Why don't you tell us what happened at that location?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: While we were sitting in the van, I don't remember exactly whether I heard it over the radio or on a Motorola, but it was stated that the Muslims that broke through towards Tuzla had confiscated a vehicle with heavy machine-guns on it and that they had taken several policemen from Doboj prisoners. I don't know if they were civilian policemen that these Muslims had captured or whether they were military policemen. After a few moments had gone by, from this building, Brano Gojkovic, Aleksandar Cvetkovic, and a Lieutenant Colonel whose name I didn't know, and two policemen, came out. They had patches with the "Military Police Drina Corps" on them. They came out of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, did you see the insignia that said "Drina Corps Military Policemen" on the two policemen who came out with Brano Gojkovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And you said a Lieutenant Colonel came out as well. How do you know that the individual who came out with two military policemen from the Drina Corps was a Lieutenant Colonel?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: He had insignia denoting officer rank on his chest. That individual had the insignia of officer rank, with the rank he actually was, on his chest, on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And that rank, again, was Lieutenant Colonel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
