utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Erdemovic, after these men came out, what happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Brano came. We had opened the door of the van, and you would open it sideways, with a sideways motion. He told us to shut the door. And when we asked him where they were going, he said that we would be escorting the Lieutenant Colonel who was in front of us, in an Opel Kadett vehicle in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would Brano be escorting? The way I understood your testimony, the way it was interpreted to me, Brano would be escorting the Lieutenant Colonel. Was it the other way around; in fact, the Lieutenant Colonel would be escorting members of your unit to a location?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. Our vehicle followed the Lieutenant Colonel and those two policemen who were in front of us, in the Opel Kadett car in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: We went in the direction of Zvornik, from Zvornik towards Bijeljina. And not long afterwards we turned off the road, the Zvornik-Bijeljina road, we turned left onto a macadamised road surface -- it wasn't an asphalt road -- and we arrived at a farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I have Prosecutor's Exhibit 24/7, which is a large panorama, placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm going to show you this image, Mr. Erdemovic, and ask you if the location that's shown on Prosecutor's Exhibit is the farm where you arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If you could place that on the ELMO, if you could, Mr. Usher, and if you could move it slowly across the ELMO so the people in the audience could also see this location.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So this is the location that's depicted in this panorama where you, the two Drina Corps military policemen, the Lieutenant Colonel, and your group arrived. By the way, did the Lieutenant Colonel have any insignia on his uniform -- was he wearing a uniform, in the first place?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What kind of a uniform was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: He had the uniform of the Army of Republika Srpska. I don't remember about his pants, but I know that his shirt was a summer shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did he have any kind of insignia denoting what particular unit he was a member of?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, after you arrived at this farm, what happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The Lieutenant Colonel and the two policemen got out of the car. The Lieutenant Colonel went into this building here [indicates], where some men were there, that I didn't know who they were. I think it was an office belonging to those people who were working there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How long did he stay in there?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Not long. Maybe two or three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: After that they all went; all those people who were there moved away. Only the guard remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When you say "all those people," you mean all the people who were working at the farm?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were on the farm. Whether they were all working there, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How many people who had been present at the farm remained after these other people left?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Just one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: After that, when they had all left, the Lieutenant Colonel was talking to Brano and I heard him say that buses would be coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As soon as he said that, it wasn't long after that, he left with these two policemen in a car. Then Brano came back to us and told us that buses would come with civilians from Srebrenica on them. And I and some others started objecting, saying, "What are we going to do there?" And he said that we would have to execute those people. In the course of this debate, the first bus was already arriving. This may have been 20 minutes later or half an hour later. So the first buses came in about half an hour, as he had said. When the first bus arrived -- I know about myself; I don't know exactly about the others, what they said -- I said that I did not want to do that, that I cannot do that, that that is not the task of our unit. Brano told me then, "If you won't do it, stand up with them or give them your rifle, and you will see whether they will shoot you."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When the first bus arrived, it parked here [indicates]. It parked here [indicates], where we see the green tractor-trailer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Which is, for the record, near a building that appears to have many openings in it and appears to be the building that is on the farthest right of the panorama. So there's a green tractor-trailer on the left-hand side of that building, in between a larger building that's a farmhouse with a red tile roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So that's the location where the buses parked. Would you continue with your testimony, please, Mr. Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When the first bus arrived, Brano told us that we had to deploy in a line from this garage here [indicates], from this building, in a straight line, perhaps 100 metres long. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You mean 100 metres away from the building that has the openings and the tree next to it? You had to deploy 100 metres past that building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Into an open field?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Please continue, Mr. Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Then I saw two policemen taking men out, men who were in the bus, and these two men were probably the security for the transport of these men, and they reached Brano and Vlastimir Golijan. And the first group of people were brought behind this garage down there, maybe 100 metres away, maybe more, but roughly to such a position. Then Brano told us to form a line. The men in front of us were ordered to turn their backs. When those men turned their backs to us, we shot at them. We were given orders to shoot.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did Brano also shoot?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did all of the members of your unit, the ten people who had been sent over there, did they all shoot?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Continue, please. Actually, Mr. Erdemovic, let me ask you some questions at this point in time. Did the buses that you saw coming to the Branjevo Farm, did they have any kind of markings on them that you could identify?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: There were markings of "Centrotrans Sarajevo" and "Drinatrans Zvornik," transportation companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: After this first group of ten prisoners was executed, what happened, Mr. Erdemovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Brano and Vlastimir Golijan, we again formed a line to secure the path, and Brano and Golijan went for the next group of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The second group was brought, and they were lined up immediately behind those first group. Our backs were turned to the garage and we were moving in the direction of the garage. And that is how groups were brought in: Men again turned their backs to us and we shot that group of people who were in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And then I take it another group was brought for execution, and they were executed as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And is that how the scene repeated itself throughout the day?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, only I have to say that the last group of the first bus, or at the beginning of the second bus, I know that Aleksandar Cvetkovic and Brano had the idea to speed up the execution so that we could use a machine-gun, an M-84.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What happened with that M-84 machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Then Aleksandar Cvetkovic took this machine-gun, positioned it, and started shooting at the group of ten. However, because the ammunition was what it was, the people were just mutilated and wounded, and they begged to be finished off.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Then a hot argument ensued between me, Brano, Slovenac, Goronja, and Aco, because some people could no longer listen to those men pleading to be killed, and we were saying if they have to die, why couldn't they die decently, peacefully, rather than being mutilated and hit and insulted and hurt? And then they put away that M-84 machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Erdemovic, were any of these men who were brought down to be executed blindfolded, did they have their hands tied, or do you recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can only remember that in the first bus they were blindfolded and their hands were tied, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, the policemen who escorted these buses of prisoners who were being brought to the execution field, could you see any insignia on those policemen?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were the same insignia as were worn by the previous two policemen who came with that Lieutenant Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What did that insignia say?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The military police of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, could you describe to the Judges the role that these Drina Corps military policemen had in the execution process that was taking place on the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of the transport, they probably guarded the prisoners and escorted them in buses. When they reached the farm, they took out ten men at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So they segregated the groups of ten that were passed on to members of your unit, and then those men were walked to the execution field and murdered, and then another ten individuals had been selected by the members of the Drina Corps military police, taken off the buses, and were waiting to be transported to the execution field. Is that how it worked?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, approximately how many buses arrived at the Branjevo farm on the 16th of July, as best as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, because those were terrible moments for me, I think between 15 and 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What time did the executions start in the morning of the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think around 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What time did they end on that same day?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: 3.00 or 4.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, how many people do you estimate, Mr. Erdemovic, were executed at the Branjevo farm on the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think about 1.000, 1.200.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your unit, the members of the 10th -- all of the members who went on this assignment, including Brano, participated in those executions, did they not?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: At some point in time, Mr. Erdemovic, did you have a conversation with one of the victims and attempt to spare him from the fate that awaited him?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That man, as soon as he got off the bus, started saying that he had helped some Serbs to get out of Srebrenica and reach the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and he was showing some pieces of paper with the telephone numbers of those people. I took him aside and told him, "Come here." He did. I started talking to him. We spoke about what had happened in Srebrenica. I let him light a cigarette. As there was a tap, a water tap not far, and I think I also gave him some water to drink. I was sorry and I wanted to save that man and others, but I selected him because he said that he had saved Serbs in Srebrenica and helped them to reach the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and I thought that I might save him thanks to that. However, not long afterwards, Vlastimir Golijan came, he took the man, and then Brano came too. And I said, "Why don't we investigate and see whether this man actually did what he said," to save him, and they said as one that they didn't want to have any witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was that man executed?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think Vlastimir Golijan killed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Erdemovic, did you see Brano Gojkovic order the bus drivers, who were transporting these prisoners to the Branjevo farm, to do anything?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After the second bus, or the first -- I don't know exactly -- they started drinking and the spirits started to have their effect. And then Vlastimir and Brano were saying that the drivers could also be witnesses, and I know that one of the drivers did shoot at a man and Brano gave him a gun to do that. He shot at a man.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Shot at him or killed him?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: He shot at him. Now, whether that man died straight away, I don't know, I can't remember, I can't say. But he did shoot at him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, did the 10th Sabotage Unit members who had gone to this farm kill all the 1.000 to 1.200 people, or did another military unit arrive at the Branjevo farm arrive at some point during the day and participate in the executions?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: All the members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment did not participate in these executions. About -- between 1.00 and 2.00, members came from Bratunac, so that I heard when somebody said that people from Bratunac had come to assist. And they took over the killing of those people, in the same way as our group had done, only they recognised some of those people and they took it out on them. I think that one of the men from Bratunac was a native of Srebrenica and he recognised some. I remember he recognised the butcher from Srebrenica, and I know that he said, "You're a good man, but I have to kill you. I know that you were not a nationalist."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Before we explore that, I want to correct a part of the record that is in the transcript. The record says at 12:09:01, "All of the members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment did not participate in these executions." I understood your testimony to be that all of the members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment did participate in executions but didn't participate in killing all of the people who had been executed on the 16th of July. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, just a second. He said, "The people who came from Bratunac." He said "people". Were there also military people or --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I was going to get to that, Judge Riad, and I'll explore that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'd like to explore now the identities of these people who came from Bratunac. First of all, Mr. Erdemovic, how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They were, as far as I could remember, all dressed in uniforms of the army of Republika Srpska. Only one was wearing a uniform that I would see and that I recognised as being the uniform of the American army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who was it who said, "The men from Bratunac have arrived"?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was Brano, but I'm not certain. I think possibly it was him, because I saw him first shake hands with them. Some people recognised each other. Aleksandar Cvetkovic was there, and I saw that they knew each other from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, did it appear to you that the men from Bratunac knew some of the people who had been brought from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In fact, you recounted at least one conversation between one of the men who was from Bratunac and the butcher from Srebrenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you conclude, based on your observations of the interactions between the men from Bratunac and the victims from Srebrenica, that these were local people who knew each other?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you describe to the Judges how the people from Bratunac acted toward the victims from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They beat them from steel rods. They kicked them, they hit them. They forced them to pray in the Muslim way. They simply took it out on them. They humiliated them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In addition to the conversation between the man who knew the butcher, did it appear that other members of the Bratunac group knew other victims who were from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask that the three next exhibits, Prosecutor's Exhibit 173, 174, and 175, be shown to the witness, placed on the ELMO, and distributed to the Judges, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, can you identify, in this image that was taken in Potocari, one of the individuals from Bratunac who was present and participated in the execution at the Branjevo Military Farm on the 16th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: This one here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you point to his face, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating, for the record, in Prosecutor's Exhibit 173, the man who is on the far left-hand side of the image. He has a bandana on his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you turn to the next exhibit, please, 174? Do you see one of the men who participated in the executions at the Branjevo Military Farm on the 16th of July in this particular image?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This one [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is that the man who appeared in the previous image?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating, on Prosecutor's Exhibit 174, a man on the far right-hand side of the image, wearing a camouflage uniform and wearing a bandana on his head.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Lastly, let me show you Prosecutor's Exhibit 175. Do you recognise the man in Prosecutor's 175?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who is that man?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: He's the same man who was at the farm that day, only in this case he's in civilian clothes. But I remember him well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: He's the same man who was wearing a bandana in Prosecutor's Exhibit 173 and 174; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm finished with those exhibits, Mr. Usher. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, after the arrival of the men from Bratunac, did members of your unit also participate in the continued killings that were taking place at the farm?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say regarding everyone, but I know that four men did not continue to participate.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who were those four men who did not continue to participate?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Myself, Franc Kos, Marko Boskic, and Zoran Goronja.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I please have Prosecutor's Exhibit 158 placed back on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did one member of your unit, Mr. Erdemovic, brag to you how many men he had killed at the Branjevo Military Farm?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is Stanko Savanovic, number 3. He said that he had killed between 200 and 300 men, that he had counted them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So the man who is marked number 3 in that exhibit was a participant in the execution squad with you, and he told you that he had killed between 250 and 300 of these individuals; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. I'm finished with that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, what was the age range of the people who were murdered at the Branjevo Military Farm?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I could tell, between 17 and 60 or 70.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How were these people dressed?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They were all in civilian clothes, except for one who had camouflage pants.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did any of these people offer resistance of any kind to the execution squad or to the Branjevo -- I'm sorry, the Bratunac Brigade soldiers who were present?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, one man. I think when they had just arrived, he started running, trying to escape, and they caught up with him and killed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, were Drina Corps military policemen escorting each and every bus that came to the execution fields?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, while the last bus was coming to the execution field, did anyone else appear with that bus at or about the time of the arrival of that bus?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question once again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'll ask it a different way. Did the Lieutenant Colonel who had escorted you to the Branjevo farm return with anybody else later in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He came at the end, when these men from Bratunac were emptying the last bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And he was present when these executions -- the last bus of people were being executed?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was he accompanied by anybody else when he came to the farm?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: There were those men who were there before, those two military policemen who were there when we headed for the Branjevo farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Tell the Judges what happened when he arrived at the Branjevo Military Farm.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: We were sitting down against the wall of the building on the farm that I showed you on the picture. Then these men from Bratunac were still taking people and killing them. Brano, Savanovic, and Cvetkovic were close to the bus, I think. The Lieutenant Colonel went towards them, over there. We were talking, and just then somebody asked the guard where the people would be buried, and he said they would be buried there, and he also said that people had been buried there before. Now, I don't know whether he meant before the Second World War, before this war, what exactly he meant. Not long after that, this Lieutenant Colonel and Brano came, Aleksandar Cvetkovic, Savanovic, and he said that we had to go to the nearby club where there were 500 Muslims from Srebrenica who wanted to break down the door. Four of us said that we wouldn't go there to do that, that we'd had enough, that we were nobody's killing machines. Brano said, "Why?" We just said we didn't want to do any more, that enough is enough. And then the Lieutenant Colonel turned around and went towards those men from Bratunac, and after a minute or two, or five -- I don't know -- they got into their vehicles and left. And we were still at the farm. There was the machine-gun and all the weapons. When we were loading it into the van, we heard the sound of gunfire coming from that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Coming from which direction?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: From the direction -- well, you see, the farm, when you're coming from Zvornik, you come across that farm, the Zvornik-Bijeljina road. You first reach the farm and then this place on the road to Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me ask you: Did all of the men who had participated in the killings at the Branjevo farm leave the farm to go to another location where people had to be killed?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The people from Bratunac went straight away. But Brano told us in the car that that Lieutenant Colonel had said that we ought to attend a meeting at a cafe in that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Before we get into the next set of killings, I want to just ask you: How many men from Bratunac were there who had arrived to participate in the killings and then went to another location to continue with the killings?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps ten, perhaps more, perhaps one or two men less. I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Before we leave the Branjevo farm, I'd like you to take a look at another exhibit, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 24/2, which is an aerial image that has markings on it. I ask that that be placed on the ELMO. Mr. Erdemovic, you've seen this picture in my office before?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, this is an aerial image of the Branjevo farm; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Does this show the location where the people who had been executed fell?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Does this image accurately reflect the location of the buildings and the bodies from the executions on the 16th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember this building [indicates] and this other one [indicates]. I don't remember this one so well [indicates] but I do remember this one and the one over here [indicates]. I recognise that that is the farm and the place where the people were taken from the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, are there other locations where people were executed beside the area with the large oval that says "Bodies"?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think these people from Bratunac, those first people were taken off here [indicates], this area here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating for the record the area to the left of the word that says "Bodies," in between -- slightly above the word that says "Wheel." In that area, there were additional bodies. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, thank you. I'm finished with this particular exhibit. Let's turn our attention back now, Mr. Erdemovic, to the departure of the people from -- the soldiers from Bratunac who left and went to a particular location. As you were leaving, you said you could hear shooting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How soon after the departure of the soldiers from Bratunac was it that you left the Branjevo farm?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps some 10 minutes later, perhaps 15, thereabouts; 10 to 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: We went in the direction of Pilica, the place of Pilica, which is where that cafe was located, the coffee bar where we were to have a meeting with that Lieutenant Colonel that Brano told us about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Describe the scene to the Judges as you entered this particular village where a cafe was located.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When you come from the Zvornik direction, the cafe is on the right-hand side. It is the Zvornik-Bijeljina road. The cafe is on the right-hand side, at a place called Pilica, and I think that is at the entrance to Pilica itself. Opposite the cafe was this other place, and when we came in front of the cafe, in front of this building on the other side, we saw people lying down on the ground, lying around on the ground, and you could hear shots.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you hear detonations from grenades as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Afterwards, when we'd already entered the cafe you could hear detonations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a number of exhibits and ask you to identify the various locations that you are going to be testifying about. If we could start first of all with Prosecutor's Exhibit 25/15, and then we will turn to 25/2, 25/5, and 25/7. While we're getting those exhibits, Mr. Erdemovic, how far apart was the cafe from the location where shooting was taking place?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I would say about 70 to 100 metres. I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We're going to start by placing on the ELMO, Mr. Erdemovic, Prosecutor's Exhibit 25/15. You mentioned the cafe. Does this picture show the cafe where you and other members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment went after you left the Branjevo Military Farm?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is this the cafe -- and did you remain in this cafe while killings took place at a location across the road?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you remain in that cafe until the killings that took place across the road finished?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn to the next exhibit, 25/2. Mr. Erdemovic, can you point out to the Judges -- first of all, you've seen this picture in my office prior to testifying; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you point out to the Judges first the cafe, where you and other members of your squad were sitting, and then point out the location where the killings were taking place.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating, first of all, the building that has the sign "Cafe" above it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Where did the killings take place?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating the cultural hall to the bottom part of the image.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, let's take a look at the next picture, please, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 25/5. What is this building?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: This reminds me of that hall in Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Is this the location -- what happened at this location, Mr. Erdemovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Over here [indicates], I can't show you exactly, but somewhere here to the right [indicates], when we arrived, upon our arrival in front of the cafe with the vehicle, that's where the bodies were lying down on the ground, and shots were heard inside over there, but I didn't go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Let's turn to our last exhibit, which is 25/7.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. There should be one more exhibit. We should have 25/2, 25/5, and 25/7. There should be three exhibits. Mr. Usher, what is the number on that exhibit, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could turn to 25/5, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I want to lastly show you this picture. Can you show to the Judges, Mr. Erdemovic, first of all, the location where the killings took place?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: This building here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating, for the record, the building that's above the two buses that appear in the middle of the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And where is the cafe located where you and other members of your unit were sitting when the killings were taking place?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Indicating the building in the lower right-hand corner. You can only see the roof portion of that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, when you were sitting in the cafe, was there something at the location where the two buses that appear in the middle of this image?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, that's where the checkpoint of the civilian police was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now we've set the scene for the rest of your testimony, Mr. Erdemovic. Would you tell the Judges, then, what happened when you got to the cafe, who was there, what you saw, and what you heard.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When we arrived at the cafe -- when you go in, when you enter the cafe, at the entrance, on the right-hand side, I called this -- these were little separate places to sit, and on the right-hand side, this Lieutenant Colonel was sitting down with another military policeman. I didn't see the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: We all went inside. I and Franc Kos sat right next to -- sat at the table on the left-hand side, by the door. All the others went off, Brano, Vlastimir, Aco, Boskic, Goronja. And the Lieutenant Colonel said, that is, he called the man working there and told him to bring drinks. I and Slovenac, as far as I remember, had some coffee, the others were, I think, drinking brandy, and they were talking. I didn't listen to what they were saying. You could still hear the shooting, and the detonations were heard at that point in that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: "That building" being the building across the street.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How long did you remain there -- I'm sorry. How long while you were there did you continue to hear shots and detonations coming from the building across the street?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Not long. Between 15 and 20 minutes, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Now, after 15 or 20 minutes, what happened, Mr. Erdemovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, that man came, the one that I have already showed you with the bandana on his head, from Bratunac, he came inside and said that everything was over, and then the others came in as well. And they talked to the Lieutenant Colonel for a while, and then we said that we wanted to go home. And not long after that we got up, got into our vehicle, and went off. And I remember that the Lieutenant Colonel just said, "Those who survived survived."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I take it at this second execution site, which was in this town, no members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment participated in those killings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The killings that took place at this particular location were committed, as far as you could see, by the men from Bratunac, who were dressed in the military uniform of the army of the Republika Srpska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Erdemovic, you said you wanted to -- you asked to leave. Did you, in fact, then leave the location of the cafe shortly after the killings that had taken place across the street occurred?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We went in the direction of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did all of the members of the execution squad from the 10th Sabotage Detachment return to Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you know where the men from Bratunac went?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you know where the Lieutenant Colonel went?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you know where the military policemen from the Drina Corps went?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Now, after your return to Vlasenica, did you eventually return back to your base in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When we returned, not much time went by, they said a bus would come to take us to Bijeljina, and that's what in fact happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, after these killings took place, you remained with members of your unit, first of all, in Vlasenica briefly, and then in Bijeljina, and you had an opportunity to converse with other members of your unit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, did you hear at any time, in your conversations with your colleagues, that members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment had participated in the separation of men from women and children in Potocari that occurred on the 11th and the 12th of July? Did you ever hear anything from any of your colleagues that they had participated in that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you ever hear, Mr. Erdemovic, in talking to your colleagues, that members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment had participated in the detention of men in Potocari, in Bratunac at various locations, at the Luke school near Kladanj, in the Petkovci school, or the Grbavci school, or the Pilica school, or the Rocevic school?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So you never heard any of your colleagues talking about that.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. But some of these places, I heard of them for the first time later on, when your investigators questioned me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Now, since your group was a reconnaissance group, Mr. Erdemovic, did you ever hear that members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment reconnoitred to find suitable detention facilities where Bosnian Muslims from Srebrenica were detained prior to being executed?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that members of your unit participated in being guards or providing security for Bosnian Muslim prisoners who were detained at various sites prior to their execution?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you ever hear that members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment participated in mass executions at the Kravica warehouse, at Orahovac, at a dam, or at a location Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you ever hear, Mr. Erdemovic, that members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment participated in the burial or the operation of heavy equipment of victims from massacres that took place at the Branjevo Military Farm, at the Kravica warehouse, at Orahovac, at the Dam, or at Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, to your knowledge, I take it that your understanding was that your unit participated in the executions only at the Branjevo Military Farm; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And I heard later on, when I left hospital, because after Srebrenica I was wounded and I was in a hospital in Bijeljina, first of all, and then at the military academy hospital, I heard rumours going around that individuals had been in the Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. But you didn't hear any rumours about those people participating in executions at Nova Kasaba, did you?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Erdemovic, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Judge Riad, Judge Wald, I've concluded my direct examination of Mr. Erdemovic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You said you had two hours. So you've concluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have concluded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I would like very much to express my admiration. We will adjourn for 20 minutes and resume at 1.00. Mr. Erdemovic, you know from your experience that now the Defence counsel will ask you some questions. I would like to seize this opportunity to tell you that the Bench appreciates very much you're coming to testify. We are adjourned until 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic or Mr. Petrusic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours, my learned colleagues of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Erdemovic. Mr. Erdemovic, can we say that you became a member of the Republika Srpska army in Dvorovi?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did you then sign an agreement with the army of Republika Srpska as to your membership in the army?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Not then but afterwards. Well, when Pelemis joined in October 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us something about that contract or agreement.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I read it out, I had it in my hands, and it was between me, as a member of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, and the Main Staff, as far as I know, of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So that contract was between you and the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska, to make matters quite clear.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So we can say that you were a professional soldier of the army of Republika Srpska, were you not?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, by signing that contract or agreement, you could put it that way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, I should now like to ask you some technical questions. We're speaking the same language, you and I, so please make pauses between the question and the answer.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I will do so. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, do you know whether the other members, and I'm speaking of the Drina Corps specifically, individual brigades, Milicka, Bratunac, Bircka, Zvornicka Brigades, whether their soldiers had the same kind of contract with the army?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can we say that the command structure of your unit with respect to superiority was made up of the following hierarchy: We had Colonel Salapura as the top man, top officer; then we had Major Pecanac; then we had First Lieutenant Pelemis and Kremenovic, whom I think was in charge of the rear for your detachment; followed by two platoon leaders, Lule of the Vlasenicki and Franc Kos of the Bijeljina platoon.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: That is all correct. But Kremenovic was not in charge of the rear, he was Pelemis' deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Can we then say that at the top of that pyramid, according to this chain of command, was the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the intelligence staff of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And by the same token, the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In a military hierarchy of this type, in the command sense or in actual, practical terms, or in any other sense, you didn't have any links with the Drina command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: When you went on assignment to the zones of responsibility of other corps, in addition to information at the command level saying that you would be passing through, you continued to be under your command; that is, your platoon was under the command of Mr. Pelemis, was it not? I can't see an answer on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So nobody else was able to issue orders to you except for your command.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, can it be said that you didn't have your own area of responsibility, in fact?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: When other units joined you in your operations, in the particular case of the mine near Srebrenica, did the members of that unit come under your command, the same command as you?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They were not directly under our command, but they were attached to us just to show us the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So their command could not issue orders to you.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And could your command issue orders to them?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if they were attached to us for that occasion, then probably our commander could issue orders to those men who were attached to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: This relationship, at what level did it function? At the level of Pelemis command or a higher level?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I only know that if Pelemis was with us, then he could command those men. If it was someone else, then he would be the one. Now whether there was a link between Salapura, Major Pecanac, and the brigade command, of the people who were attached to us, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, I think you said, and please correct me if I'm wrong, that on the 10th of July you headed from Bijeljina, towards Zvornik, towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And you arrived in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: How many members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment were boarded onto, I suppose, some trucks or buses in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Between 15 and 20, into a small bus. I don't know exactly now but between 15 and 20. That is what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You reached Bratunac on the 10th. What time of day was it, roughly?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe 2.00 in the afternoon. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Could you please describe your movements from Bratunac to the position in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the area well but I know that we went a roundabout away through woods and over hills. I know it was a difficult route for us to take. Our group and the group from Vlasenica were led by two three-barrelled guns belonging to the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Was there a total of 15 of you, including you and the group from Vlasenica, or was the Vlasenica group independent?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. You asked me, "How many of you started from Bijeljina" and I said between 15 and 20. But when we got to Bratunac, shortly after that these men from Vlasenica came.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: How many of them arrived?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I think there was a total -- when we left on the 11th [sic] for Srebrenica, there must have been about 30 of us, but I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You reached the area above Srebrenica on the 10th, in the evening. Were you then under Pelemis' command?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Both platoons.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In the morning, on the 11th of July, who gave you orders to go to Srebrenica, into the town itself?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Milorad Pelemis, the commander of our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, were there with you members of the regular units of the Drina Corps? I mean members of the Milici, Bratunac, Zvornik, and Vlasenica Brigades.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: There were about 15 men from the Drina Wolves which, as far as I know, were billeted in Zvornik, and they came under Pelemis' command because he went into town with us then. They were attached to our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You were divided into several groups. Can you tell us how many?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, our unit was divided into four groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Were members of the Drina Wolves with you in those groups?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No, they were not mixed up with us in those groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So they were not under Pelemis' command either.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, judging by the way Pelemis spoke to us, I gathered that Pelemis could give them an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Those members of the Drina Wolves, did they have their leader?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: At that location?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: The leader of the group was certainly with them, the Drina Wolves.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know who that leader was?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, it's not Legenda.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No, Legenda was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: In your examination-in-chief you mentioned the order that you should guide the population towards the football stadium.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Pelemis told us -- people asked, "What if we come across civilians?" He said that we should direct the civilians to go in front of us towards the football stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So you didn't come across civilians, rather, your group didn't.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we came across a couple. Throughout that period there may have been 200 civilians that we came across, elderly people, women, people who couldn't move quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Did you see them go to the football pitch?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They went in front of us so I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know that that football pitch, viewed from Srebrenica, is in the direction of Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: At the time I didn't know. I do now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So you know the location where it is now.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, today I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Could you conclude today that they went in the direction of Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When I reached the centre of town, what I thought was the centre of town, I think they took the road towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: After a certain amount of time, after the bombing raids by NATO forces, you were given orders to withdraw to one of the checkpoints at the entrance to Srebrenica, on the southern side.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When we reached this second mosque, upon entering Srebrenica, Pelemis said that everything was finished and that members of various units were coming down from the hills -- I don't know exactly which units they belonged to, but they were coming down -- and Pelemis said we shouldn't move forward any more but that we should go back to where we had started out from entering the town, and to guard the entrance to the town. On the way there he told us to inform him when General Mladic and the others arrived. He didn't say who the others would be. I just remember him mentioning General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: The road that you took on the way back, is that the road that General Mladic came along?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Three vehicles came. First was a Mercedes belonging to the former JNA. Mladic was sitting in front, and I didn't recognise the other persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: From the position where you were at that checkpoint, could you see how many troops had entered the town?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how many, I can't say now, but in my estimate there must have been 500 or 700 soldiers maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And they passed by your checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, they were coming down from the surrounding hills. And before the vehicles that passed were two APCs, a self-propelled and a Praga, as far as I can remember, but not many troops passed that checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: At that checkpoint you spent the night.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Not at the checkpoint itself. It was not a checkpoint. We were protecting the entrance to the town. I learnt here that this was the southern side of Srebrenica. Yes, we spent the night there in houses, a big house, I remember, and a smaller house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: The order for movement the next day, the 12th of July, between 10.00 and 12.00, came from Pelemis.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. A man who sometimes drove Pelemis, under the name of Zoran Stupar, came and said that that Pelemis had ordered us to move towards Vlasenica. We were already supposed to go and search this mine, one at the entrance to Srebrenica and the other coming out at the Bratunac side, and we were informed that we should go to Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So Stupar is conveying Pelemis' orders to you.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And Pelemis previously had issued orders that you should search the mine.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When we got down into town, after a few minutes a man came, I think his name was Garic, from Vlasenica, and the mine was in his area. He asked Pelemis, as we knew the mine, that we should work there. We should have done that the next day but we didn't. I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Let us go back for a moment to the 11th again. Your comrade from the detachment, I think the young man whose funeral you attended later, when he described General Zivanovic as a drunk, when he said, "He's not a General, he's not a commander, he's a drunk," did he mean "pijano," meaning drunk, did he mean a person who is frequently drunk? Is that what the term implies?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: That is what it sounded like to me, and since I saw him drinking brandy from the jerrycan, that is how we describe a man who drinks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So he wanted to describe him as a person prone to alcohol, and thereby that he shouldn't have the role he has as a commander.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it sounded like.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, how many members of the 10th Detachment left Srebrenica and went towards Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, all the members of the unit, on the 12th, left.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Therefore, some 30 of you.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. May I just say, we didn't see Pelemis when we left Srebrenica, we met him on the way somewhere, towards the south, where there was this former UNPROFOR checkpoint, south of Srebrenica. We found him, Cico, and another two soldiers there, who were with an APC that you saw on the video clip which they had seized from UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So your group went south of Srebrenica, Zeleni Jadar, that is, the mine, Milici, and then the road goes on to Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that area too well, but when we passed I could see that there were open cast mines. So possibly those were mines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: But regardless of your knowledge or not of the area, there's no doubt that you went to the south of Srebrenica, in the direction of Vlasenica. On that road, did you see members of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: On the 16th of July you left Vlasenica via Zvornik, towards the farm, and then you saw a certain number of members of the police.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know under whose command they were?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I just saw the emblem. It said, "The Military Police of the Drina Corps." I don't know exactly under whose command they were. The name of the person or his rank, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know how units of the Drina Corps were deployed at the time in their area of responsibility, on the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know that at the time another operation was under way?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that over the radio, that the Muslims, who were going from Srebrenica, were breaking through towards Tuzla and that they had managed to capture a Praga or a self-propelled gun, and several policemen from Doboj. I don't know whether they were civilian police or military police, or whether they were really from Doboj. But that is what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know, and had you heard that on the 16th of July there were other combat operations in Zepa?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You came across a Lieutenant Colonel in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Could you describe him, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: He was tall, I would say about a metre and 90 centimetres, heavily built. He had a rather big head. He had -- I don't know how to put it. It was very sunny that day, very hot, and he had a cap. As far as I could remember, he had greying hair and a receding hairline.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Erdemovic. Are you sure, Mr. Erdemovic, that he had the rank of Lieutenant Colonel?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with your permission, I should like to show 28/15, Prosecution Exhibit, on the ELMO for identification purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, the officer whose head has a circle around it in red marker, is that the person you saw?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Members of this unit, or rather the soldiers who came to the farm from Bratunac, as you said, did they tell you that they were from Bratunac, or did they specify the unit they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I heard this when Brano, I think it was Brano who said, "Men from Bratunac are coming to assist." I don't know exactly whether they were from Bratunac, nor did I talk to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So it was not stated that members of such and such a brigade were coming, but simply men from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, when all this was over in Branjevo and Pilica, you returned to Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: So eight of you went to Branjevo and Pilica and eight of you returned.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Where were the members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment from the 12th until the 16th, when you returned?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, there were 30 of you who reached Srebrenica. From Srebrenica you all returned, with the exception of this young man who got killed, you got to Vlasenica. From Vlasenica, eight of you went to Branjevo and Pilica. Where were the others, the other members of the detachment, in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I have to explain. I don't know where they were on the 13th, 14th, and 15th, when I went to the funeral. On the 16th, as far as I remember, they all stayed behind me in Vlasenica, and when we returned to Vlasenica we saw them all there, because a few minutes after that we went to Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: You stayed at the VMA, the military medical clinic in Belgrade, when you were being treated for your injuries, and you said that you heard some things there. Did you hear anything about the movements of the 10th Sabotage Detachment at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I definitely heard about the case of Nova Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I heard that these persons from my unit were there, and this was recounted by somebody -- to my wife and she passed it on to me, that Velimir Popovic, Brano Gojkovic, Milorad Pelemis, that they were in Nova Kasaba, that they took a man, a young boy, who reported and said that he had 100.000 German marks in a house in Srebrenica, that they took him there, he found the money, and that they killed him. And when I came home, I heard the same story from Marko Boskic, telling some people.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Is that all that you heard about the movements of the members of the 10th Sabotage Detachment during the time when you were not with the rest of them?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I heard later, my wife told me again, that they had gone looking for gold. I don't know about that for sure, but I think this could be true, because Marko Boskic told the same story a second time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, do you know which unit was located in Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have finished my cross-examination. Mr. Erdemovic, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Petrusic. Mr. Erdemovic, first Mr. Harmon, would you like to ask some questions? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have only a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, you were asked by my colleague questions about the joint operation between your unit and the Drina Wolves that took place in the direction of Srebrenica on the 11th of July. My first question relates to an answer you gave in my direct examination. You identified the leader of the Drina Wolves as a man named Legenda. Do you remember that answer? You have to answer aloud.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, members of the Drina Wolves -- did it appear to you, when you were making the assault on Srebrenica, that members of your unit were working together with members of the Drina Wolves in making the assault in the direction of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: It appeared to me that they were working in cohorts, that Pelemis did have contacts with Legenda, which he probably did have in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did Legenda -- let me ask that question differently. To your knowledge, was Legenda a participant in the operations that were being directed against Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw that on the pictures, the video first, and later on you showed me a photograph and I identified it as being Legenda.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I want to focus your attention back to the time when you were participating in this operation, that is, the 11th of July. Were you aware that Lieutenant Pelemis was in communications with Legenda?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I did know because Pelemis said that we should set fire to the first thing we came across on the left, on the right. There was a haystack next to me and I should set the haystack on fire. He said that we should set it alight so as not to be hit by the artillery and Praga and those heavy machine-guns that were positioned up on the hill. And I do know that that was done -- that Legenda, in fact, was at that elevation point.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So Legenda was at a location near Srebrenica where he could cover your operations with some kind of heavy fire if necessary; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct. And I also know because of another example. When a bomb was thrown, we heard over the radio, our signals officers had said that a tank had been damaged, and the vehicle, a vehicle of the commander of the Drina Wolves, Legenda. A bomb fell on that hill where that communication line was located, and Legenda himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Are you talking about a NATO bomb that fell?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And did the NATO bomb hit a location, as far as you're aware, that was near a vehicle that was operated or owned by or used by Legenda?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. Judge Wald, would you like to ask your questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, as your unit was moving into Srebrenica on the 11th, I think you testified on direct that you didn't meet much resistance, but I wanted to make sure I understood correctly. Is that right? In other words, was there resistance from Muslim forces or other forces as you moved into the centre of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. There was -- well, I can't say there wasn't any resistance. You could hear shots shooting, but there was no great resistance of any kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: All right. Now, did your unit, during that same movement into the centre of Srebrenica, did your unit, or later on any of the other units which came down into the town, engage in setting any of the houses on fire or individual searches of the houses that were in the area?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, only one house was burnt and it was at the entrance, when you enter the town from the south side. It was close to the mosque, and it was when the NATO planes had already thrown their bomb. And of course the members did take part in the search -- in searching the houses and buildings in the town of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: At that time was anything done during the period that your unit was in Srebrenica to the mosques, either one?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No. Only from the first mosque, the flag had been lowered, taken off the mosque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Moving on to Branjevo. You said that in the course of the afternoon, something between 1.000 to 1.200 people, you estimated, were killed. Were the bodies just left as each unit of ten -- as each group of ten was brought to be executed? Were the bodies of those that were already executed just left there, or during the period you were there, did any kind of loading and carrying away of the bodies, putting them on trucks, et cetera, take place?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So in other words, as each new group of ten came up to be executed, they were brought up to the place where they could see all the bodies of the people who had been previously executed just lying there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Incidentally, were the drivers of the buses that brought the victims to the Branjevo Farm, you mentioned that at one point it was said, "We don't want them to be witnesses," were they civilians? Were they police, military, what? The drivers of the buses that brought the victims.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I only know that they drove civilian buses. Whether they were members of the military or not, I can't answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So you don't remember whether they wore any kind of distinguishing uniform or just civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Now, when you got to Pilica, you showed us where the cafe was and it was across the state from the Pilica Dom where the detainees were kept inside. Now, this was, I gather, in the middle of the afternoon. Were there any other people around in the area? This is the middle of town, as I understand it. Besides the group that was with you in the cafe and the people who were inside the Dom across the street, there were no ordinary townspeople around?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there were people there. Between these two buildings there was a checkpoint of the civilian police, and people did pass by in cars. And right next to the hall, there were houses, inhabited ones. Yes, there were civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: So there were some people around on the streets while this was happening.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Traffic was passing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: You told us, I believe, that you heard the shots, and later detonations, inside the Pilica Cultural Dom across the street. Did you see people attempting to escape or being shot outside the Dom, in front of the Dom, or did you just hear the sounds that were going on inside, while you were in the cafe?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When we arrived at the cafe, and when we turned off from the main road to get in front of the cafe to park the car, I saw people in front lying on the ground. While I was in the cafe itself, I heard shooting and bombs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: But did you actually yourself see anybody being shot and fall in front of the Pilica Dom?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. My last question. You and some of your colleagues from the 10th Unit were brought to Pilica, and then you say you went into the cafe and you sat down, you waited, and soon somebody came and said words to the effect that, "Well, it's over, and those who have survived have survived." Did anybody ever explain why they brought you there if all you were going to do is sit in the cafe and watch from across the street?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't see what was actually happening across the street. Nobody had told me anything, told me why. We were just told that there was to be a meeting of some kind, but as I noticed, there wasn't any meeting. A man from Bratunac came and said that everything was over, that it was finished. When he came and said this, the Lieutenant Colonel got up and said, "Those who have stayed alive have stayed alive." I don't know why he said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: My last question would be: Roughly what is your estimated number of the bodies that you actually saw outside the Pilica Dom?
