utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say with any certainty, but perhaps 10 or 15. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Wald. Mr. Erdemovic, I would like just to follow with you a little bit some of the phases of these unfortunate events. You said when you came into Srebrenica, at first they met a civilian who pleaded that he was not in the army and still Mr. Pelemis ordered to slit his throat. That was just at the beginning. What was the purpose, really, of that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it happened, as far as I was able to see, in Srebrenica, in the centre of town, where the second mosque was located. What the purpose was of that killing I could only assume. I assume that it was because perhaps he was of an age for the army, an age for military service. I don't know, actually, what the purpose was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Was it to intimidate the people? I mean, just a sign to show them what's going to happen to them? What was the reason?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot say that. I just cannot say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: It was in front of all the people. It was in broad daylight.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was. It happened in front of the soldiers. There were no civilians there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: There were no civilians. Now, then they called on the people to move to the stadium. Were men and women included, or was it just for the men?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: From the very beginning, when we moved into town, we called out to people, if there was anybody in the house to come out, because the houses would be searched, and we were told that we weren't allowed to fire at civilians. So we called out to any civilians there, to come out of their houses and to move towards the stadium. This was at the entrance to the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: All the people, you called on all the people of Srebrenica to move to the stadium.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, from all the houses, if there was anybody in the houses, but there were only some 200 people, in my assessment, who came out of those houses. They were invalids, elderly people who found it difficult to walk, elderly women.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And they moved to the stadium too?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: They were moving in front of us. I don't know where the stadium was or if it existed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Were they included in the execution? These people who you said were old, the infirm, those who could not walk, they also went to the buses, to the execution?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You didn't see that. But what kind of people were being executed then, exactly? Any women between them, to start with?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Any old people?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I already said that they were between the ages of 17 and 60 or 70 years of age.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Between 17 and 70. Those who were not between 17 and 70, what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But you were there.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Please could you explain your question. I know I was there but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: What happened to the people who were not executed? Were they left to stay at their homes? What happened to them? If everybody had to go to the stadium, was there any separation, or did everybody have the same fate?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: All those people who had remained in their houses when we entered the town, they were told to come out and move in front of us in the direction of the football stadium in Srebrenica. But I never reached that stadium, nor did I actually see this separation, the separation of these people, the individuals there. I just said that I know that the people that were brought to the farm were between the ages of 17 and 70.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You mentioned also that Stanko Savanovic was bragging that he killed between 200 and 300 men, and the squadron, the killing squad, was about eight people. You who were killing, you were eight?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: If you count, then I think that reach -- was it a competition of who would kill more?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that was it. Actually, he did it -- some people, after the first shooting, would fall down but they were not actually dead, and later on he would finish them on with his pistol.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: There was also shooting, as you said, by machine-guns and people were not killed, they were hurt and some of them were not killed. Were they all finished after this?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, and Stanko Savanovic did most of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: There were no survivors, because you said the Lieutenant Colonel said, "Those who survived have survived." Were there some survivors, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say now whether there were or weren't. I didn't examine all the people to be able to ascertain that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I think you mentioned something about -- when you mentioned about the cafe, you said after 15 minutes you were in the cafe and a man came and said everything was over. What did you understand from that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that the execution in the Dom was over, and I didn't hear any more shooting after he had said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So it was clear that he was speaking of the execution.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: Well, to me it was clear that he was speaking of the execution because nothing else could have been over, finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Do you have an idea of who was in the Dom?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC
utterances.text: When that Lieutenant Colonel came towards the end, when everything was drawing to a conclusion at the Pilica farm, he said that there were 500 Muslims from Srebrenica who wanted to break through, so that I concluded that they were Muslims from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, thank you very much. Your testimony is over, and I repeat that we appreciate your coming. Thank you very much. You will now go out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just ask a question of the President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Yes. And also I will request that if you have anything to add, you are welcome to add it, whether it's a question or whether it's any statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to say that everything that occurred in Srebrenica, that against Mr. -- that is to say, General, against the General, I don't know him and I don't know that he issued any orders. And I should like to thank his Defence counsel for their correct and proper conduct towards me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Would you like to say anything else in general about your experience?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope that it is not repeated ever again to anyone. That it doesn't happen to anyone ever again, that is my greatest wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: We share very much this wish. Thank you very much, Mr. Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, we have ten minutes to go. You can use them the way you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I would first like, Mr. President, Judge Riad, and Judge Wald, to introduce the exhibits that have been testified about by Mr. Erdemovic, and if I could move into evidence, then, the following exhibits: 28/17, which is a photograph; a film, which was Prosecutor's Exhibit 145; 147, which was a photograph; 148, which was a film; 152 through 157, which were photographs; 158 as well, which was a photograph; Prosecutor's Exhibit 28/4; and Prosecutor's Exhibits 170 through 175, which were photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. I assume that the Defence counsel has no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We have no additional evidence today, Judge Riad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: As I've mentioned before, tomorrow I will be the Presiding Judge, and we'll resume exactly our testimonies in the same way. So we'll start tomorrow at 9.30. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: 2.03 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 23rd day of May, 2000, at 9.30 a.m.
